summary: Re-verified master-file rename propagation (iteration_31 bug fix) across backend + UI. The whitespace/case bug is FIXED: _propagate_master_rename() now uses an escaped, case-insensitive '^\s*name\s*$' regex and all 6 PUT endpoints call it. 25/25 rename pytest cases pass (16 existing + 9 new edge cases covering leading/trailing whitespace + case mismatch for all 6 master types, regex-metacharacter names, prefix-match safety, and a trim-migration assertion). Trim migration 'v1_trim_loan_fields' is recorded and 0 of 8 loans retain untrimmed values in any of the 9 text fields. UI e2e confirmed: admin login -> Master File -> rename customer 'Vishwa' -> 'Vishwa Renamed' -> Month MIS -> expand Apr-2026 -> row shows 'Vishwa Renamed' -> reverted to 'Vishwa' (verified in DB). NEW BUG FOUND (pre-existing, unrelated to propagation): all master POST/PUT duplicate-name checks interpolate the raw name into $regex without re.escape, so names containing '(' or '[' return HTTP 500, and names with '*'/'+'/'\' bypass the duplicate check and then 500 on the unique-index DuplicateKeyError.

critical.issue: Duplicate-name check does {'name': {'$regex': f'^{name}$', '$options': 'i'}} with the raw user-supplied name (19 occurrences: server.py lines 2448, 2468, 2501, 2506, 2559, 2633, 2648, 2680, 2695, 2723, 2738, 2766, 2781, 2809, 2824, 2856, 2872, 2908, 2923, 2954, 2969). Two failure modes reproduced: (1) name containing '(' or '[' -> pymongo OperationFailure 'Regular expression is invalid: missing closing parenthesis / missing terminating ] for character class' -> HTTP 500 on both create and rename (e.g. a realistic name like 'Ravi (Delhi)'); (2) name containing '*', '+' or '\\' -> regex is valid but does not match the literal string, so the duplicate check passes and the unique index name_1 raises an unhandled DuplicateKeyError -> HTTP 500 instead of 400. Fix: wrap with re.escape(name) everywhere (as already done correctly in _propagate_master_rename and the bank migration) and catch DuplicateKeyError -> 400.

minor.issue: Endpoints still return only {'id', 'name'} and never the propagation count, so the UI cannot tell the user how many loans were updated (toast just says 'Updated' even when 0 loans matched). _propagate_master_rename already returns modified_count - surface it.
Dead variables: `result = await db.master_*.update_one(...)` is assigned but never used in all 6 PUT endpoints, and `updated = await _propagate_master_rename(...)` at line 2477 is unused.

The contact_no propagation still uses exact equality: update_many({'customer_name': name}, ...). It runs AFTER the rename so it matches the new name, but it is not whitespace/case tolerant like the name propagation - inconsistent with the fix.
Ordering: the duplicate-name 400 check runs before the existence lookup, so a duplicate name submitted against a non-existent id returns 400 instead of 404.

issues: Leftover QA data still present (reported in iteration_31, NOT cleaned): loan 1b7600b1-ef70-4aeb-a0cd-605c05da6e58 (customer 'Vishwa') has bank 'TEST_Replace_Bank_1'; master_banks still contains TEST_Detail_Bank, TEST_Replace_Bank_1, TEST_UI_Bank_1 and master_companies contains TEST_Co
BANK column is truncated ('TEST_Replac...') with no tooltip/title attribute, so the full value is unreadable

action_items: Apply re.escape() to the name in all 19 master duplicate-name $regex checks (server.py lines listed above) - currently names with '(' or '[' cause HTTP 500 on master create AND rename.
Catch pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError in master create/update handlers and return HTTP 400 'name already exists' instead of a 500.
Return the propagated loan count from the 6 master PUT endpoints and show it in the Master File toast (e.g. 'Updated - 3 loans renamed') so a 0-match rename is visible to the user.
Make the customer contact_no propagation whitespace/case tolerant for consistency with _propagate_master_rename.
Remove the dead `result =` / `updated =` assignments in the 6 master PUT endpoints.

Clean leftover QA data: master_banks TEST_Detail_Bank / TEST_Replace_Bank_1 / TEST_UI_Bank_1, master_companies TEST_Co, and fix loan 1b7600b1-ef70-4aeb-a0cd-605c05da6e58 whose bank is TEST_Replace_Bank_1.
server.py is 3397 lines - split master-file, loans and MIS routers into separate modules.
critical_code_review_comments: _propagate_master_rename() is implemented correctly (re.escape + '^\\s*name\\s*$' + case-insensitive) and is reused by all 6 PUT endpoints - the DRY duplication flagged in iteration_31 is resolved.
The same re.escape hygiene applied inside _propagate_master_rename and the bank migration was NOT applied to the duplicate-name checks - that inconsistency is now a live 500.

The trim migration only normalises loan_applications; master_* collections and the Excel import path are not trimmed, so a future import can reintroduce untrimmed loan values. The regex matching makes renames tolerant, but the MIS grid will display the raw untrimmed value. Consider trimming in the import/create path too.

_sync_loan_to_master() does not sync agent_name to master_agents, so agent renames only propagate when the master agent was created manually (confirmed by test: the agents edge-case test had to create the master entry explicitly).

success_rate.backend: 100% on rename propagation (25/25); 30% on regex-unsafe master names (3/10) - separate pre-existing bug

rca_of_the_issue: Original whitespace bug: RESOLVED. _propagate_master_rename() matches loans with {field: {'$regex': '^\\s*'+re.escape(old)+'\\s*$', '$options':'i'}} so Excel-imported values with surrounding whitespace or different casing are now updated, and the one-time 'v1_trim_loan_fields' migration normalised existing rows (verified: 0 untrimmed across 9 fields in 8 loans). New 500 bug RCA: the master create/update duplicate-name checks build the case-insensitive regex by f-string interpolating the raw name. MongoDB compiles that server-side, so '(' or '[' produces an invalid-regex OperationFailure (code 51091) surfacing as HTTP 500; '*', '+' and '\' produce a syntactically valid but semantically wrong pattern that fails to match the literal name, letting the insert through to the unique name_1 index which raises an uncaught DuplicateKeyError, also a 500. Reproduce: POST /api/master/customers {'name': 'Ravi (Delhi)'}.
